posts.name: Nielzabub
posts.cooked:
MarioFanaticXV:

The problem is that Final Fantasy VII was a very graphics-driven game; it primarily sold off the FMV cutscenes, which at the time were quite rare in console games. Any graphics-driven game tends to become rather underwhelming as time goes on. Now if you go back and play V which was driven by gameplay or VI which was driven by the story, then you can still enjoy them greatly even if you have no nostalgic attachment to it, but VII was ultimately forgettable for anyone that didn't grow up during that era.

I'm not sure how much I can agree with this given the large fanbase Seven has managed to acquire. The use of cutscenes was definitely a factor in Seven's success, but part of it is also how those cutscenes were combined with the gameplay to create an epic experience. Now, not everything about the story is perfect, Disc 3 is just mostly filler, but it was good enough to keep people engaged. The game also still has one of the best introductions I've ever seen. You instantly know the genre, the main character, and the world aesthetics and conflict all while learning how to play the game in a way that's intuitive, fun, and doesn't feel overwhelming. 

 

While the graphics are dated, people's love for the game isn't. Fans of the series hold on to it just as much as Six or Five. As far as the remake goes, the only main thing I hope they change is to make it so that your Limit command doesn't replace Attack. I'd actually like to see elements of Ten's overdrive system incorporated.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
I like IV the best, I also love V, and XII is fantastic too.

FF VII had some great characters, the strength of the game was the team, you felt their personalities, and you liked them.  The plot wasn't amazing, but the characters for the most part were.

Then you have the sidequests.  They really made the game, so much to do, so many ways to delay the story and just have fun with your team.

My point is that the new game won't improve the good things, and will likely have to alter them to keep them relevant with new graphics.  I honestly think this game being remade will take away from its appeal more than give new players access to the great game it was.

Think of the saucer games, are they going to leave that all the same gameplay with better graphics?  I can't imagine that.

The best parts of the game can't be improved, the cutscenes can, but at that point why not make a series instead of the game.

I think the remake will not displace the original, no matter how they dress it up.
